newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks swing back to close modestly higher.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks swing back to close modestly higher.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed the first trading day of the year modestly higher on Monday, as selective buying of shares in blue-chip companies helped the market, which was still suffering from an uncertain outlook for the economy, dealers said.
They also said that the market had been depressed earlier in the morning after the dollar hit a near 46-month high of 117.00 yen, but losses were limited.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 average finished the half-day session up 84.65 points or 0.44 percent at 19,446.00. It earlier dipped to 19,203.53.

"The market was discouraged at the opening by the yen's easing during the new year holidays in Tokyo. But since the fall had been more modest than expected, people started to buy on dips," said a trader at a major Japanese securities house.

Masaaki Higashida, deputy general manager at Nomura Securities Co Ltd, said that the market had anticipated the yen's easing against the dollar at the end of last year and early this year and that the impact on the stock market was limited.
"There has been worry over the weaker yen, and the (stock) market factored it in to some extent," he said.
Turnover was about 161 million shares at noon, up slightly from the 149 million shares at the end of the half-day session on December 30, the last trading day of 1996.
In other indices, the broader TOPIX index gained 9.92 points or 0.67 percent to 1,480.86. The Nikkei 300 average was up 2.19 points or 0.78 percent at 282.45.
Advancing issues outpaced decliners 574 to 430, while 188 issues were unchanged.
Gainers were led by precision instruments, oil, credit/lease, communicatons and pulp/paper. The major losers were fisheries, transportation equipment and railway/bus.
Shares in some blue-chips saw solid buying.
Toyota Motor Corp shares climbed to a record high. The share price ended 20 yen higher at 3,350 yen, its highest level ever.
Shares in NEC Corp gained 60 yen to close at 1,460 yen, in the heaviest volume of 6.78 million shares on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Sony Corp also jumped, ending up 110 yen at 7,700 yen. Ricoh Co Ltd was up 30 yen to close at 1,360 yen.
The second section index was 4.75 points higher to close at 1,829.21, with 3.49 million shares being traded.
The over-the-counter (OTC) index was up 2.56 points at 1,333.11.
